results.summary: This design is a decimal counter that increments from 0 to 9 once per second and drives a 7-segment display. A 4-bit counter wraps at 9, and combinational logic decodes the value into segment patterns on outputs uo[0] through uo[6], with uo[7] as the decimal point. The design expects a 1 Hz clock input, configured via clock_hz: 1 in info.yaml. It is a simple educational example of counter and decoder logic.

This project is a minimal 32-bit RV32I RISC-V processor core based on the bit-serial SERV architecture, which trades throughput for very small area by processing one bit per clock cycle. It is designed for low-resource applications and is compatible with an FPGA project from BGM infrastructure. The core is implemented in Verilog and is intended for ASIC implementation. It is notable for its extremely compact design suitable for Tiny Tapeout.

This project is a VGA color test image generator that outputs a test pattern to a VGA display. It uses a finite state machine and counters to generate the necessary timing signals and pixel data. The design is implemented in Verilog and is intended for educational purposes. It demonstrates basic VGA signal generation and display output.

This project is an ALU design written in VHDL that includes arithmetic and logic operations. It supports addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division, along with an instruction decoder to select the operation. The ALU is implemented using standard cell logic and is suitable for educational purposes. It demonstrates combinational and sequential logic design.

This project is a clock generator and timer circuit that drives a 7-segment display. It uses counters and a clock divider to produce timing signals. The design is implemented in Verilog and is intended for educational purposes. It demonstrates counter and display interfacing.

This Wokwi project is described as a counter driving a 7-segment display, with four input pins and seven output pins. It is a simple 2-bit counter that shows its current value on a 7-segment display. The design uses a counter and decoder to display the count. It is an educational example of counter and display logic.

This Wokwi project is a simple 2-bit counter that shows its current value on a 7-segment display. The counter increments on each clock edge and wraps around after reaching the maximum value. The output is decoded to drive the 7-segment display. It is an educational example of counter and display logic.

This project is a shift register and ring counter design that drives a 7-segment display. It uses a shift register to generate patterns and a ring counter to sequence them. The design is implemented in Verilog and is intended for educational purposes. It demonstrates shift register and counter applications.

This Wokwi template project reads up to seven lever inputs and displays the corresponding number on a 7-segment LED, with a reset button to clear the display. The documentation is largely placeholder text, so the exact behavior of the outputs is uncertain. It is intended as a template for educational purposes. The design uses a decoder to map inputs to segment patterns.

This project is a VGA color test image generator that outputs a test pattern to a VGA display. It uses a finite state machine and counters to generate the necessary timing signals and pixel data. The design is implemented in Verilog and is intended for educational purposes. It demonstrates basic VGA signal generation and display output.
